what: Does NFL coaching behaviour drift over time, and does a recency-aware training scheme predict the next season better than full history? (the owner, 2026-11-27, after R5: 'Investigate whether the trailing-quarterback-pull discrepancy represents broader changes in NFL coaching behavior over time ... Do not hand-tune the problematic substitution situation.')
written_before: any walk-forward score of any candidate on any table was computed
data: nflverse play-by-play 2016 to 2026 week 12 through R2's compact loader (R1's seal: 2026 week 13 on is never read); players.csv for positions; regular season only
folds: S = 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 (full regular seasons) and 2026 weeks 1-12 (the last development fold); each fold trains on seasons 2016..S-1 and scores season S

tables.T1_call: pass (dropback: pass, sack, scramble) vs run on scrimmage plays downs 1-3, cell = quarter (1-4, OT as 4) x offence margin bucket (<=-17, -16..-9, -8..-4, -3..3, 4..8, 9..16, >=17) x down x distance bucket (1-2, 3-6, 7-10, 11+) x field zone (own 1-20, 21-50, opp 49-21, opp 20-1) -- R1's call table's dimensions
tables.T2_nohuddle: no-huddle on scrimmage plays, cell = quarter x margin bucket x (last 2:00 of the half or not) -- R1's tempo table
tables.T3_clock: clock runoff between consecutive scrimmage snaps of the same drive and half: 1 when the game clock ran 35 s or more, cell = quarter x margin bucket x (last 2:00 of the half or not) -- R1's clock-by-phase table (35 s is a measurement split near the running-clock median, not a model threshold)
tables.T4_rb_target: a targeted pass goes to a running back (RB/FB) rather than a WR/TE, cell = down x field zone x margin bucket -- R2's who-gets-the-ball table
tables.T5_pull: the starting quarterback's pull at each identified drive, R3's s6 logistic form (nfl_coach_sim_r3.features), every candidate refitting its coefficients

not_studied: R4's shifts: ~70 pulls a season, every shift estimated on 400+ pooled pulls; a one-season fold cannot score a training window
cell_model: a table cell's rate is (successes + 20 x the pooled rate) / (trials + 20), the pooled rate the same candidate's weighted overall rate

candidates.exp: season weight 0.5^((S-1-s)/h), h chosen per fold from {0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16} by the summed log loss of predicting each training season from 2018 on from the seasons before it (a nested walk-forward; never S)
candidates.rw: hierarchical: the full-history cell rates (or the logistic's coefficients) as the shape, plus a league tendency -- a logit offset common to every cell -- that follows a season-level random walk: each training season's offset estimated by maximum likelihood with its sampling variance, the walk's innovation variance tau^2 fitted by maximum marginal likelihood (Kalman filter, grid), and the forecast for S the filtered level after S-1

score: held-out log loss summed over a game's rows (both teams); a candidate's gain = full's loss minus the candidate's, per game; SE over games (clustered by game), every fold pooled

decision.table_drifts: a non-full candidate's pooled gain on the table > 2 SE and positive in at least 5 of the 8 folds
decision.scheme: the candidate with the largest gain summed over the five tables per game, if that sum > 2 SE and no table's gain is below -1 SE; else full history stays
decision.half_life: descriptive: per table the fixed h on the grid with the lowest pooled walk-forward loss, and the rw's fitted tau beside the offsets' sampling SD
decision.consequence: nothing is built into R1-R5 (pinned). A winning scheme becomes R6's training scheme under its own registration on fresh games (2028+, or 2027 with the dependence stated: the owner's call)
